verdict_line: WELL-FORMED (record only — Preflight is not implemented, and `war check` does not run gates)

retitled: WAR-SAS-RQ-001
Every WAR has immutable UUIDv7 identity
Document identity is stable; legacy UUIDs are preserved and new shared identities should use UUIDv7
WAR-SAS-RQ-002
Local aliases do not substitute for global identity
Local aliases do not substitute for source identity or authority
WAR-SAS-RQ-003
KF allocates official enterprise identity
Selected federation authorities allocate their official enterprise identity
WAR-SAS-RQ-004
Registration does not silently transfer Source Holder
Registration and import do not silently transfer source ownership
WAR-SAS-RQ-005
Cross-repository relations resolve through KF federation
Federated cross-repository relations retain their issuing and local authorities
WAR-SAS-RQ-010
Authored atoms are directly editable sources
New documents and legacy authored atoms remain editable sources before immutable approval
WAR-SAS-RQ-011
Bound atoms are edited only through their owning authority
Bound source content changes through its owning authority
WAR-SAS-RQ-012
Generated atoms and parents are not directly editable
Generated views are regenerated from sources rather than edited as authorities
WAR-SAS-RQ-013
Composition is typed, ordered, and deterministic
Document composition is typed, ordered, and deterministic
WAR-SAS-RQ-014
Full WAR Markdown and canonical JSON compile from one Basis
Human and canonical machine views derive from one captured source basis
WAR-SAS-RQ-015
Required atom omission fails closed
Missing required source content prevents a complete task packet
WAR-SAS-RQ-020
Every normative decision is a first-class ADR
Material governing architecture decisions remain first-class ADRs; in-scope advice is not a new decision
WAR-SAS-RQ-021
ADR Overview is generated
Decision indexes are generated from source records
WAR-SAS-RQ-022
WARs trace to SAS requirements and Roadmap
Work traces to applicable SAS requirements; no SAS or roadmap is required for every valid prototype draft
WAR-SAS-RQ-023
Child WARs cite exact parent revision
Child Warrants cite their exact parent basis
WAR-SAS-RQ-024
Childs do not rewrite parent rationale
Children do not rewrite parent rationale
WAR-SAS-RQ-025
Supersession preserves old WAR and marks it non-current
Successor work preserves earlier Warrants and their historical standing
WAR-SAS-RQ-030
Authorized Contract Revisions are immutable
Approved contract snapshots are immutable
WAR-SAS-RQ-031
Progress cannot amend contract
Progress cannot amend a contract
WAR-SAS-RQ-032
State is decomposed into phase, condition, outcome, currency, standing
State separates lifecycle, execution condition, result, currency, and acceptance or qualification standing
WAR-SAS-RQ-033
Material amendment creates new revision
Material amendment creates a new contract revision
WAR-SAS-RQ-034
Prior attempts retain original contract basis
Prior attempts retain their original basis
WAR-SAS-RQ-035
Readiness requires Preflight
Workflow readiness checks its required inputs; document validity is separate
WAR-SAS-RQ-036
A delivered artifact of a resolved WAR changes only through a recorded correction
Successor work preserves old delivered bytes and evidence without freezing a live pathname; corrections remain separate
WAR-SAS-RQ-040
Milestones and stages are distinct
Milestones and execution stages are distinct
WAR-SAS-RQ-041
Stages use named typed ports
Typed stage ports remain a selected orchestration adapter contract
WAR-SAS-RQ-042
Stateless actors receive one Stage Dispatch
An executing actor receives an exact task dispatch basis
WAR-SAS-RQ-043
Dispatch contains exact basis, capabilities, resources, outputs, stop conditions
Task context exposes basis, required outputs, constraints, limits, and stopping conditions
WAR-SAS-RQ-044
Agent authority is explicit and bounded
Execution authority is explicit and bounded by human-approved effective policy
WAR-SAS-RQ-045
Replay, repair, and restart are distinct
Replay, repair, and worker recovery retain distinct attempt history and limits
WAR-SAS-RQ-046
A Dispatch declares its token estimate and budget; exceeding the budget is a refusal
Entry token estimates include rendering overhead; exceeding a required-content budget is a refusal
WAR-SAS-RQ-050
Completion summary decomposes into obligations
Assurance qualification decomposes completion claims into bounded obligations
WAR-SAS-RQ-051
Claims declare bounded scope
Claims declare scope bounded by their evidence
WAR-SAS-RQ-052
Evidence, observation, inference, judgment, resolution remain distinct
Claim, evidence, observation, inference, judgment, acceptance, and qualification remain distinct
WAR-SAS-RQ-053
Performer reports cannot satisfy independent gates
Performer reports cannot satisfy independent verification
WAR-SAS-RQ-054
Required unknown gate results block resolution
Required unknown or failed checks block assurance qualification
WAR-SAS-RQ-055
Controlled work requires adequacy review
Assurance requires adequacy evidence with applicable refusal and control cases
WAR-SAS-RQ-056
Gate Definitions are separately governed and versioned
Required check definitions and expectations are versioned and protected from performer changes during verification
WAR-SAS-RQ-057
Gate invalidation propagates to dependent resolutions
Invalidated evidence changes dependent qualification standing without rewriting history
WAR-SAS-RQ-058
Residual risk requires sufficient judgment authority
Residual risk requires explicit authorized human acceptance and cannot waive a failed baseline requirement
WAR-SAS-RQ-059
Resolution binds exact contract and assurance snapshot
Human acceptance binds exact contract, result, and assurance evidence
WAR-SAS-RQ-060
KF owns authority and lifecycle
Knowledge Fabric owns authority and lifecycle for its selected federated workflow, not every standalone compiler use
WAR-SAS-RQ-061
Liminal owns document semantics and Basis
OpenWarrant owns standalone standard and context compilation; Liminal is an optional adapter
WAR-SAS-RQ-062
Katana owns agent runtime and PromptIR
Selected Katana adapters retain Katana runtime and PromptIR ownership
WAR-SAS-RQ-063
BLUT owns typed computational execution
Selected BLUT adapters retain BLUT typed execution ownership
WAR-SAS-RQ-064
OpenWarrant does not duplicate those kernels
OpenWarrant compiler does not require or duplicate sibling runtime kernels
WAR-SAS-RQ-065
Native systems retain artifact authority
Native systems retain their artifact and source authority
WAR-SAS-RQ-070
CLI works file-native and offline for drafts
Reference authoring and compilation work offline without a model
WAR-SAS-RQ-071
`war plan` returns a structured proposal
Agent-assisted planning returns reviewable structured source proposals
WAR-SAS-RQ-072
Agent proposals are validated before writes
Proposals are validated before source writes and cannot grant themselves authority
WAR-SAS-RQ-073
Planner creates ADR drafts for normative decisions
Planning identifies material architecture decisions for ADR proposals
WAR-SAS-RQ-074
`war check` is deterministic and agent-free
Document and compiler checks are deterministic and agent-free
WAR-SAS-RQ-075
Generated views are drift-checked
Generated views are checked against their exact source basis
WAR-SAS-RQ-076
KF commands use typed actions, not direct status edits
Federated controlled actions use the owning authority interface rather than direct status edits
WAR-SAS-RQ-077
Work of three kinds — code, document, run — has a registered gate and a walked example
Selected code, document, and run workflows each require their own observed gates and examples
WAR-SAS-RQ-080
Canonical portable WAR is RFC 8785 JSON
Canonical structured preservation uses RFC 8785 JSON
WAR-SAS-RQ-081
Cross-system WAR digests use explicit algorithms and domains
Digests use explicit algorithms and versioned domains; original source bytes remain recoverable
WAR-SAS-RQ-082
Export includes contract, sources, receipts, assurance, resolution
Preservation exports retain contract, sources, receipts, assurance and acceptance when present without inventing missing history
WAR-SAS-RQ-083
Export-import-export preserves semantic identity
Export-import-export preserves semantic identity and original evidence bytes
WAR-SAS-RQ-084
Historical superseded, disputed, and annulled records remain available
Historical superseded, disputed and annulled records remain available
WAR-SAS-RQ-085
Every ssh-signed act leaves an attestation a foreign verifier can check
Existing SSH-signed acts retain their portable attestations and original subjects
